definition: A personal, accumulated collection of proven instructions, kept and refined the way a cook keeps recipes; a promptwright’s working grimoire.
etymology: After playbook and spellbook — but chiefly a revival. The promptbook was a real object of the Victorian theatre: the stage manager’s marked copy, from which the play was actually run.
in_context: Hang on — that one’s in my promptbook.
the_case: Everyone finds the phrasing that works and then loses it. What is missing is not effort but an object — a place to keep the instructions that earned their keep. A restored word carries an authority a freshly minted one has still to earn.
seo_title: promptbook — the file where you keep your best AI prompts
seo_description: Everyone working with AI ends up with a scratch file of prompts that worked. Calling it a promptbook makes it a practice: kept and refined, like recipes.
